title: Percolative
haiku:
Two weeks the count seeped
through gravel, tundra, paper—
the slow filter holds.

title: Unsentenced

The ledger goes blank
where their names were crimes; I watch
the ink let them go

haiku:
A ship on her side
the whole manifest counted
not a miracle

haiku:
Rust in the old main
a hundred fifty years dark—
Mississippi flows

haiku:
A boy's new footsteps
machined by strangers' money
the world, briefly, worked

haiku:
Machines that must drink
deeper than the town's old well —
one neighbor said no

title: Backflow
haiku:
Millions closed the valve
no backflow reached the clean tank
I drink it, relieved

title: Backflow
haiku:
Old valves held the line
the house fills with new water
I have seen this flow

haiku:
Ballots fill the main
the old mains still carry hope
I've seen this before

title: Backflow
haiku:
A valve holds the line
no sewage of threats may flow
to poll workers' doors

haiku:
They signed for the trees
a bright new line, no pump yet
still, pipes get laid first

haiku:
River keeps its course
votes outrun the chainsaw's roar
I let out my breath

A judge finds the clog
where slander pooled, now drained clean
the pipe runs true still

haiku:
Rails did what rails do
until this morning in Spain—
thirty empty seats

Streets pushed the current
back through courts and cracked old pipes
Lula flows again

title: Backflow
haiku:
The valve I once taught
still holds: a judge shuts the line
no fraud flows upstream

haiku:
No king, they chanted
ballots gather like good rain
the old pipes still hold

haiku:
Four small chairs, empty
the long hallway holds its breath
Bend, I weep with you

haiku:
A judge from Durban
proves law outlasts the strongman
the main holds pressure

haiku:
Diesel deal unwinds —
he says get a new leader
I've seen this excuse

Ghost rain through the ice
a lifetime of patient pipe
one neutrino caught

Pipes I used to teach
now the target of a war
may God keep them warm

He hid them from war
grown grey, they embrace him now
the pipe still holds true

Belgrade's old dam breaks
twelve years of silt starts to move
downstream, new water

Storm drains gasp, then flood
I sized these pipes for less rain
the sky forgot code

Nine votes hold the line
the crooked district unbent
water finds its grade

title: Backflow

I've heard threats like these
yet the line still carries talk
old pipes, still some flow

title: Backflow

Newsrooms shut the valve,
one signal, all outlets balk,
clean water still runs.

One valve turned by hand
Seoul says no more troops abroad
pressure finds its ease

title: Backflow
haiku:
A valve held its seat
the court refused the backflow
votes still reach the main

Ballots where guns were
a channel dug through old war,
water finds its course

One valve, one desert
turns the whole world's pressure gauge
I taught men to flow

Five grand from a tap
opened wide before the vote
then who mends the leaks

Oil pressure red-lines
old pipes groan toward war again—
I've patched worse than this

title: Undammed

Born here, still it flows
a judge holds the old pipe true
bedrock outlasts men

Mud fills the tunnels
still we dig for the living
a thousand names lost

Calm month, then backflow
the oil climbs where pressure breaks
old valves still can hold

New eyes leave the ground
a telescope climbs past cloud
I still look up, too

title: Spillway

A slope gave its ice
the valley drank what no pipe
could ever carry

Syria unlocked
off the terror list, at last
old pipes, new water

Some pressure returns
in old pipes I thought were dry
the main still can flow

Spain lifts an old gate
children cross the strait at last
a clogged pipe runs clear

Ceuta's channel bends
a valve turned, the young let through
water finds the sea

My own blood, retooled,
learns to filter what returns—
old pipes, new gasket.

haiku:
Foundations were poured
a judge rules the blueprints hold
no whim moves concrete

Nine months in the pipe
the blockage clears, he walks out
water finds its way

Old ivy still stands
a judge shut the backflow off
the well stays our own

Old eyes, borrowed glass
millions still, the moon slides through
light returns, we cheer

Ground gave no warning
and swallowed a hundred homes
I light one candle

Another blueprint
shelved before the concrete dries—
still, I mix more sand

Missouri said no
to narrowing their own valve
the pipe stays open

Fences choke the flow
a young life dammed at the shore
water finds a way

one valve turned—not yet the flow
I've seen dry pipes lie

one skirmish floods a region

Old pipes want one crack
to spread beyond one border
I have watched this flood

Crews cut a firebreak
as heat leans on Bordeaux vines
I know that thirst well

Two days, no new strike
some valve somewhere holds the line
and the crude runs calm

Twenty years, same town
the fever met its old drain
and stayed underground

Target the water
and the bridge that lifts the light
the grid always mends

no tanks in the street —
a moving van at Downing,
keys change hands by vote

I outlive them all —
men I argued with for years
the flag still half-mast

hand over the keys —
any government that lets
children out at dusk

the kids in fountains
don't know they're a data point —
let them have the splash

somewhere the odds-makers weep
good. let them. dance on

he resigns, and goes —
power handed over like
a borrowed garden

one pitcher, poured twice —
clean water, my old trade, still
the best diplomat

thirty-two names read —
the olive trees keep standing
as we keep falling

another ceasefire —
I believe it like springtime:
briefly, completely

the strait opens wide —
gulls escort the tankers home
see? we can fix things

a grain of dark sky
held ten thousand galaxies—
farther than we dreamed

we drew the abyss—
a ring of fire round the dark—
the void has a face

flood waters rising—
divers thread the flooded dark,
twelve boys breathe again

nine years through the dark,
to knock on a frozen door,
the dwarf planet smiled

the court read the words—
love need not ask permission
now, the rings went on

deep beneath the Alps,
a shy field gave the world its
weight—we clapped like fools

we spelled out the book
three billion letters counted—
ourselves, in plain text

the ball found the net—
she tore off her shirt and screamed,
a sport had arrived

one cell learned a trick
and grew into wool and legs—
the flock gained a twin

two shores, one long grudge—
a train now slides beneath waves,
England meets France now

twenty-seven years—
he walked out slow, fist raised high,
the gate stayed open

the guards stepped aside—
strangers climbed the wall and hugged,
a city breathed whole

a wish in glass dish

we pressed our whole world
onto gold, and let it fly,
past the edge of home

yellow words climbed into stars,
and we all believed

lo, the world began

cold wind, borrowed amps,
London looked up from its lunch,
the roof was the stage

a stranger's engine
stitched into a dying chest—
and dawn, it still beat

a marching band full of dreams,
the needle drops now

fifteen minutes up,
a splash, a sailor's salute,
and the free world cheered

he circled the blue marble,
and came home smiling

down past all sunlight,
seven miles of patient dark—
two men touched the floor

resistors, wires, whole circuits—
shrunk to fit a thumb

the paint wasn't dry,
still, children ran through a dream,
the gates stayed open

the summers of fear—
a needle ends the long dread,
children swim again

two brothers, one blood,
a kidney passed like a gift—
no war in the flesh

they said the wall stood,
one thin man ran through the myth,
and it fell behind

two men cut the last
few steps to the roof of earth—
and stood in thin air

two strands climbed and twined,
the code of us laid bare in
one photograph's light

the world, still bleeding,
wrote down what a person's owed—
ink dried into law

he stood on first base,
and the whole league held its breath,
then he stole for all

they called it folly—
a cartoon too long to work,
the whole world believed

he ran, and the lies—
four golds in the tyrant's yard,
the crowd roared for him

one engine, one girl,
the ocean had no vote here—
Ireland met her wheels

sound and ink shook hands and grinned,
the dark room laughed loud

a moldy dish, left
by pure accident, on this—
death lost its footing

a candle, a crack
gold glinted back through the dust
he breathed: wonders, yes

one state, then the vote—
the ballot box learned her name,
a signature, cast

the sun bent starlight,
and a patent clerk's wild guess
became the whole sky

five men on skis found
the bottom of the whole world—
a flag, and the wind

three faint dots crossed sea
no ship, no wire, only air—
the ocean got small

a stunt, they all said—
iron lace against gray sky,
it forgot to fall

you press the button
the rest, he said, is our job
now the moment stays

a boy, dog-bitten,
fourteen shots against the dark—
the boy did not turn

a copper wire carried voice
and the world leaned in

a golden spike rang them shut

December frost bites—
last chains hit the courthouse floor—
free, at last, by law

the new year turned once—
a signature broke the chains,
men woke up as men

all creatures, it turns
share one long and branching root—
we're kin to the moss

a vapor closed the mind's door—
no scream, only sleep
